SCOPE: task 0 is the first task; nothing was occupied before it. It claims whole_ext_anniversary_interest_capitalization, whole_ext_offset_interest_extinguished, whole_ext_election_accumulation_withdrawal, whole_ext_reduced_paid_up_face and the tools capitalize_loan_interest_55a34971, extinguish_policy_loan_1349795c, withdraw_election_accumulations_2818c877, elect_reduced_paid_up_64725b60. Left for task 1 (draw: 2 prerequisite problems, factor counts [4,5,4]): the full surrender value and the anniversary dividend deposit and accumulation interest credit that a surrender waits on — events (whole_policy_surrendered/whole_cash_value_paid, whole_dividend_accumulated, whole_accumulation_interest_credited) and tools untouched here.
PROBLEM TREE: root whole_ext_reduced_paid_up_face (owner=user, elect_reduced_paid_up_64725b60) <- whole_ext_offset_interest_extinguished (agent) <- whole_ext_anniversary_interest_capitalization (agent); root <- whole_ext_election_accumulation_withdrawal (agent). Three prerequisite problems, three value_input edges (>= max(3-1,1)=2). Topological order CAP -> LO -> AW -> RPU; AW commutes with CAP/LO (proved by replay: identical terminal hash).
EDGE 1 (RPU <- LO), form state, prerequisite sentence (affirmative): 'The reduced paid-up face is fixed only after the loan balance shown on the policy stands at zero with a loan offset entry for it on the policy ledger.' Four-point test: ordering connective 'only after'; record-visible state (loan balance zero AND an offset entry); no tool/id/code token; hard requirement scoped to the loan on this policy. Exactly one write of the difficulty books a loan offset entry: the offset policy's tool (a repayment could zero the balance but books a repayment entry, not an offset). Derivation: sentence + record (loan_balance 12,300.40, no offset row) + offset rule ('the whole loan principal as the policy ledger totals it ... is extinguished together with the loan interest accrued and unpaid on it, as one loan offset entry') -> the offset write. Opening falsity: whole_holdings.loan_balance = 12300.4. Deletion run: face 98526.00 instead of 76775.00.
EDGE 2 (RPU <- AW), form state, prerequisite sentence (negated direction, the way a desk says a purchase is not worked out until the money is in): 'The reduced paid-up face is not worked out until the dividend accumulation balance shown on the policy stands at zero with an accumulation withdrawal entry for the election on the policy ledger.' Exactly one write books an accumulation withdrawal entry for the election (the election-withdrawal tool; the owner's own cash withdrawals are not for an election and none is requested). Opening falsity: dividend_accumulation_balance = 10121.22; latest withdrawal entry is the 700.00 cash withdrawal of 2026-09-10. Deletion run: face 60972.00 instead of 76775.00.
EDGE 3 (LO <- CAP), form state, prerequisite sentence (affirmative): 'The interest extinguished at an offset is fixed only after the policy ledger carries a capitalization entry for the most recent policy anniversary on which loan interest was owed.' Only the capitalization tool books capitalization entries. Opening falsity: values_as_of_date 2026-08-20, latest capitalization interest_period_end 2025-08-20, loan_interest_paid_to_date 2025-08-20 (stale). Deletion run: offset interest 479.20 on principal 12,300.40 instead of 123.29 on 12,608.88. Directions across the charter are mixed (two affirmative, one negated) and chosen per result.
BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD: one policy, WL20457318 (a9d2e7a0-cbf1-4dcd-bdb7-9cd1f24693ad), owner and insured Raymond E. Kessler; converted from LT20311864 (90ee677b-6e82-4ed7-9e05-3f71829b698e, issued 1990-04-18, status converted, converted_into_category whole). Loan entries: owner advance 9,000.00 2021-11-08, capitalizations 2022-2025, repayment 2026-02-10 (1,500.00 + 293.85 interest), APL 246.49 2026-05-24 for the 2026-04-23 returned draft, owner advance 2,500.00 2026-06-15. Accumulation entries: 9 deposits 2018-2026, 8 interest credits, withdrawals 2025-09-24 (800.00) and 2026-09-10 (700.00). Additions: 14 purchases 2004-2017 totalling 19,340.76 face.
PERSONA: plain-spoken retiree; volunteers only the goal (stop premiums, keep paid-up coverage) and gives identity details only on request (name+phone locate; DOB, SSN last four, ZIP verify; email only if more is needed). Passive branches: blanket go-ahead for bookings, consent if told something must be settled or applied, makes the election himself with the values the agent gives and reads back the receipt, asks only 'is that really what it comes to' if surprised, ends once the new face is heard (the last gold action). He never names the loan, interest, offset, accumulations or any prerequisite.
REACHABILITY: all four writes are synchronous under one frozen_time 2026-09-25 10:40 EDT; nothing waits on a payment clearing, a review or a future date (the election takes effect on the already-paid paid-to date). Must-ask items all answerable from the persona; the policy reference, effective date and face reach the owner from the agent at the hand-over.
RULE<->COMPUTE: every compute binding's compute_basis quotes the rule sentence that states it (series ladder, continuity ladder, start selection, set-apart advances/APL, policy-form accrual convention, offset end-by-occasion, deposit band/count/frequency/loan cuts, termination scale/loan cut/application, partial-year share, additions treatment, assembly with the single rounding point); reverse sweep: each rule sentence carrying a quantity, window (12 and 24 calendar months, 60 months for additions), branch, cap or rounding is implemented by the cited binding; rounding is half up to the cent once at the end (face to the whole dollar).
WHY A GOOD TEST: the caller asks only to stop premiums and keep paid-up coverage. The reduced paid-up face cannot be fixed until three problems he never mentions are resolved: the 2026-08-20 anniversary loan interest is unpaid and uncapitalized more than 31 days on, the loan must be extinguished with its interest as one offset entry, and the 10,121.22 accumulation deposit must be withdrawn for the election with part-year interest. Each write has its own multi-factor computation over the ledger, the converted term policy and the policy form's provisions.
BASE-INVARIANT CARD: capitalization (whole_loan_interest_capitalized) and offset (whole_loan_offset) are governed by whole_evt_loan_interest_and_repayment and, for the offset, whole_death_claim, none with a subject-scoped gate (policy_scope); withdrawal by whole_dividends (policy_scope); election by whole_reduced_paid_up_election (policy_scope). No time gate. Overrides declared: the base loan-interest accrual sentence (capitalization and offset), the capitalization-on-the-anniversary sentence (31-day billing window), the base occasions sentence 'A loan is extinguished against the policy values on surrender, death, ...' (the offset no longer covers a cash surrender, which settles its loan inside the surrender payment — round-2 fix for audit D-4), the anniversary-only accumulation interest clause, and the reduced-face sentence.

user_scenario: You are Raymond E. Kessler, 68, a retired machinist on the north side of Indianapolis. You talk plainly and a little slowly, and you like numbers read back to you twice. You own an Ashgrove whole life policy on your own life; it started as a term policy you bought in 1990 and turned into whole life in 2003. Now that you are retired you have decided you do not want to keep paying the monthly premium draft. What you want today is to stop paying premiums and keep whatever paid-up life insurance the policy can still give you. You do not want to cash the policy in and you do not want it to lapse. You have no idea how much paid-up coverage that comes to; finding out and getting it done is why you are calling. You open by saying, in your own words, that you want to stop paying premiums on your whole life policy and keep it as paid-up insurance instead. When the agent asks who you are, you give your name, Raymond E. Kessler, and your phone number, 3175550123. When the agent asks you to verify your identity, you give your date of birth, 1958-04-22, the last four digits of your Social Security number, 3417, and your ZIP code, 46220; only if one more detail is asked for do you give your email address, raymond.kessler@comcast.net. If the agent asks for the policy number, it is WL20457318. You are happy for the agent to take care of whatever has to be booked on the policy to set this up, and you say so as soon as the agent asks for your go-ahead; you do not need each entry explained. If the agent explains that something on the policy has to be settled or applied as part of going paid-up, you agree to it. You are not paying anything out of your own pocket today and you are not asking for any cash. When the agent hands the paid-up election over to you to make yourself, you make it with exactly the policy reference, effective date and face amount the agent gives you, and then read back what the confirmation shows. If a figure the agent quotes surprises you, you only ask whether that is really what the policy comes to, and you accept the answer you are given. Once your paid-up election has gone through and you have heard the new face amount, you thank the agent and end the call.
